section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
label: Tax test: employee or contractor (Inland Revenue)
value: Generally an employee if the payer controls how and when the work is done. Indicators: must do the work personally; told what to do, when and how; paid a set rate; can get overtime or penal rates; set hours; works at the payer's premises; the payer sets the standards
note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Employer's guide, IR335 (September 2026), pages 8 and 14-17

section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
label: Tax guidance: Interpretation Guideline IG 16/01
value: Common-law tests: intention, control, independence, fundamental (in business on their own account) and integration; leading case Bryson v Three Foot Six Ltd [2005] NZSC 34
note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
source_title: Inland Revenue (Tax technical): Interpretation Guideline IG 16/01, Determining employment status for tax purposes (employee or independent contractor?), issued 8 March 2016, paragraphs 5-6

section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
label: Employment law: gateway test (from 21 February 2026)
value: A worker is a contractor if all criteria are met: a written agreement saying they are a contractor or not an employee; free to work for others; can choose when to work or subcontract; can decline extra work; had a chance to get independent advice. Otherwise the common-law test applies
note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
source_title: Employment New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment): Employee or contractor

section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
label: Schedular payments: form and tax code
value: The contractor gives the payer a Tax rate notification for contractors (IR330C); the payer deducts withholding tax at the chosen or standard rate and reports it under tax code WT. Activities not listed on the IR330C have no deduction
note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Company tax (income tax on companies) [national]
value: 28% for most companies, 17.5% for Māori authorities; GloBE multinational top-up tax up to a 15% effective rate for groups with revenue over EUR 750 million (IIR and UTPR from 2025, DIIR from 2026). Paid by companies. Income Tax Act 2007; GloBE rules added by the Taxation (Annual Rates for 2023-24, Multinational Tax, and Remedial Matters) Act 2024
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax rates for businesses (last updated 1 April 2024)

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Branch profits tax or tax on distributed profits
value: No separate tax: Inland Revenue lists none. A non-resident company with a permanent establishment in New Zealand is taxed on income derived here (company rate 28%); dividends carry imputation credits
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax residency status for companies (last updated 25 June 2025)

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Self-employed contributions: ACC levies [national]
value: Earners' levy 1.75% including GST on liable earnings of $50,501 to $156,641 (2026/27); Work levy by ACC classification unit (average 0.69%). Paid by self-employed people, invoiced by ACC. Accident Compensation Act 2001
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), section 2.1; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), page 16

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Contractor rules: schedular payments (withholding tax) [national]
value: Standard rates 10.5% to 33% by activity, chosen rates from 10% (15% for non-residents), 45% without a notification; non-resident contractors 15%. Paid by contractors, deducted by the payer as a prepayment of income tax. Income Tax Act 2007 (schedular payments) and Tax Administration Act 1994
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), sections 5.14, 5.14.1, 5.14.2; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), pages 13, 16-17

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Simplified or presumptive regime for the self-employed
value: None: self-employed people pay income tax on net profit at the individual rates through an individual return; GST registration is required above $60,000 a year
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Self-employed (last updated 6 July 2026)

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Non-resident tax on employment income (PAYE) [national]
value: The income tax rates (10.5% to 39%) through PAYE plus the ACC earners' levy, without the IETC; 10.5% flat for recognised seasonal workers (NSW). Paid by non-resident employees, deducted by the employer. Income Tax Act 2007; double tax agreements may exempt
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Inland Revenue: Employer's guide, IR335 (September 2026), page 54 (Non-residents)

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Local council rates (property tax) [local]
value: Set by each council each year on land, capital or annual value; fixed charges at most 30% of rates revenue. Paid by owners of rateable land. Local Government (Rating) Act 2002
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
label: Property transfer tax or stamp duty
value: None: stamp duty was abolished (residential conveyance duty in 1988, all remaining conveyance and lease duty for instruments executed after 20 May 1999)
note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
